comparator.name: Dutch Languages and Cultures — Dutch Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The programme-specific 2026–27 Teaching and Examination Regulations define three formal routes. The registry target expressly names the Dutch Language and Culture route, so that route is selected independently of UCR fit. For students beginning in September 2026, the regulation gives a coherent 60+60+60=180 EC curriculum: 60 EC of named first-year components, 60 EC of named second-year components, and a third year comprising a genuine 30-EC minor, a 10-EC faculty-wide module, a 10-EC thesis, and two named 5-EC components. The regulation states that the second- and third-year parts of this new curriculum take effect in 2027–28 and 2028–29 respectively; they are the prescribed continuation of the 2026 entry cohort rather than a mixture of concurrent-cohort tables. The minor is retained as open curricular space and no optional minor subject is presented as compulsory.
components: Open minor space; no optional minor subject is universally compulsory.

routeSelection.basis: The University of Groningen regulation distinguishes Dutch Language and Culture, Frisian Language and Culture, and Minorities & Multilingualism. The normalized registry target itself names Dutch Language and Culture, so this formal route is selected before and independently of evaluating any UCR course fit. The route's genuine 30-EC minor remains open rather than being populated with an invented specialization.

exception.reason: This is a discipline-specific Dutch Studies degree whose compulsory spine combines Dutch phonology, syntax, semantics and language acquisition with historical and present-day Dutch, medieval, early-modern and modern Dutch literature, advanced Dutch-language proficiency, research workshops and a Dutch Studies thesis. UCR offers one introductory Dutch course plus genuine general courses in literature, rhetoric, communication and psycholinguistics, but those courses do not provide a sustained advanced Dutch-language, Dutch-linguistics and Dutch-literature sequence. Constructing a 24-course UCR schedule from the broader adjacent subjects would change the named academic field and leave the defining Dutch core uncovered.
exception.curriculumContext: The exact 2026–27 regulation accounts for all 180 EC in the Dutch Language and Culture route for the September 2026 cohort. Its second- and third-year curriculum is introduced in 2027–28 and 2028–29 as that cohort progresses. The exception is therefore based on the absence of defensible UCR curricular depth, not on uncertainty about the comparator's route or credit total.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 current rows in data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned terms. MCCCOMM112 Dutch teaches basic oral and written communication for everyday situations and cultural orientation; it is not an academic Dutch linguistics or literature sequence. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide broad literary study. MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication, MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning, MCCCOMM213 Rhetoric in Action, MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication and MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory provide adjacent rhetoric and communication work. HCBGATE102, HCBCOGN311 Higher Order Functions and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics provide adjacent cognitive-language content, while HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar and GOSHIST312 History Research Seminar provide general research support. None supplies the missing Dutch phonology and syntax progression, historical Dutch, advanced Dutch proficiency, the required sequence of Dutch literary periods, or a Dutch Studies research capstone. No defensible 24-course closest match can therefore be scheduled.
